verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both identities are stated verbatim: ∫₀¹ a_L dφ = a is '(∫ φ in 0..1, A φ) = a', and ∫₀¹ (-b_L) dφ = a⟨t⟩_{θ'} is '(∫ φ in 0..1, C φ) = a * m' together with angularMean t = m, C being loopC which the file's docstring identifies with -b_L. The only rewriting is the last link of the paper's chain: the Lean keeps the tilt mean as a free parameter m and writes the prescribed second moment as a·m, never as -b_s, so 'a t_s = -b_s' is recovered by instantiating m := t_s = -b_s/a, which is the paper's own definition of t_s in the statement of Lemma C.1. The Lean form is therefore stated for an arbitrary prescribed mean, not only for -b_s/a.
